newsitem.title: USA: Official again seeks Miami budget plan extension.
newsitem.headline: Official again seeks Miami budget plan extension.

text.p: For the second time in almost as many weeks, a Miami official asked a state appointed oversight board on Monday to give the city until September to submit a balanced five-year budget plan, citing burgeoning welfare costs and a pending referendum to dissolve the city.
Miami vice mayor Tomas Regalado asked the board, which was appointed in December of last year to help the city through its fiscal woes, at an oversight meeting here.
"It all happens between August and September. The (city) administration will be overwhelmed with the situation," said Regalado. "We just don't have the time."

The proposed dissolution measure was developed by the Miami Commission, which has until Wednesday to draft ballot language and until September 4 to hold the referendum on whether the city should be dissolved into Dade County.

Additionally, fiscal pressure is mounting as the city is scrambling to make provisions for an estimated 25,000 legal immigrants who will lose Federal benefits in September under the recently enacted U.S. Congressional welfare reforms.
Miami met the oversight board's April 1 deadline to submit a five year budget, but the last three years of the proposed budget have deficits ranging from $16 million to $42 million.
That prompted concern from oversight board members, who heard the city's detailed report on the proposal Monday.
"In the outlying years the concept need to be refined a little more," board member Cynthia Curry told Reuters during a break in the meeting.
Regalado asked the board to give the city until the end of the fiscal 1997 budget year to refine the plan. Two weeks ago the board refused to extend the deadline.
Lt. Governor Buddy MacKay told Reuters during a break in the meeting that an extension would be up to the baord, however, "I don't see any reason why they need an extension."
